ai_summary: Great Britain's wind output currently stands at 12.9 GW, with estimated Scottish wind output reaching 4.3 GW, representing 42.6% of installed Scottish wind capacity. This localized abundance of renewable generation drives Scottish carbon intensity to a pristine 0 gCO2/kWh versus 89 gCO2/kWh GB-wide. However, severe cross-border transmission constraints continue to prevent this surplus renewable power from flowing efficiently to southern demand centers. As a direct result, 67.2 GWh of Scottish generation has been curtailed so far today through Balancing Mechanism bids, incurring a substantial constraint cost of about £3,729,809. To compensate for this trapped zero-carbon energy, thermal plants were forced to ramp up elsewhere on the network, consuming an estimated 12,777,405 m3 of natural gas and releasing an additional 23,537 tonnes of CO2. Annualizing these grid bottlenecks suggests an estimated total yearly cost of curtailment of £1,361 million. When recovered across national electricity volumes, this financial burden adds an estimated £5/MWh to everybody's invoice in the UK, underscoring the pressing operational, economic, and environmental imperative to reinforce high-voltage transmission infrastructure between Scotland and England.
